journey.title: Tab out of the departure date to the passengers field
journey.goal: Tab moves focus from the date field to the next field, as in any form

functionalJourney.title: Change the passengers with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Editing another field and saving submits the saved departure date

guards.title: Escape still closes the calendar
guards.goal: With the calendar open, Escape closes it and Tab then reaches the passengers field

guards.title: Clicking the date field still shows the calendar
guards.goal: A pointer user who clicks the departure date sees the month and can pick a day

plan.root_cause: The Tab keydown event on the date input is prevented when the calendar is open, preventing focus from moving to the next form field. This occurs because the datepicker component does not handle the Tab key to allow focus to exit the input when the calendar is shown.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a keydown listener to the input that hides the calendar and allows the Tab key to proceed when the calendar is shown. This ensures that pressing Tab while the datepicker calendar is open will close the calendar and move focus to the next focusable element (the passengers field).

protected declare _onTriggerClick: () => void

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Tab key will move focus from the departure date field to the passengers field when the datepicker calendar is open, restoring expected form navigation behavior.
functional_risks: Hiding the calendar on Tab might interfere with users who wish to navigate the calendar with Tab (though the calendar's internal tabbing is unaffected as focus is on the input, not the calendar).
If the calendar is shown via means other than input focus (e.g., programmatic show), the Tab key behavior remains unchanged.
The added listener introduces minimal overhead and is properly cleaned up on disposal.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Tab when the datepicker calendar is open moves focus to the next form field.
Verify that pressing Tab when the datepicker calendar is closed still moves focus normally.
Verify that the calendar still functions correctly for date selection via mouse or keyboard.
Verify that the calendar hides appropriately when Tab is pressed (as a side effect of the fix).
Verify that no JavaScript errors are introduced.

plan.root_cause: When the datepicker calendar is open, Vanilla Calendar Pro sets tabindex=-1 on the input element to remove it from the tab order. This causes the browser's default Tab key behavior to fail (focus jumps to body instead of the next form field). Additionally, VCP likely installs a keydown listener that calls preventDefault() on Tab, preventing focus movement entirely.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a capture-phase keydown listener on the input element that intercepts the Tab key when the calendar is shown. The listener stops immediate propagation to prevent VCP's listener from calling preventDefault(), calls hide() to close the calendar (which restores tabindex), and allows the browser's default Tab behavior to proceed naturally.

edits.after:
protected declare _onOutside: (event: Event) => void
  protected declare _onTriggerClick: () => void
  protected declare _onInputKeyDown: ((event: KeyboardEvent) => void) | null = null

  constructor

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Tab while the datepicker calendar is open will now close the calendar and move focus to the next focusable element (the passengers field), restoring standard form keyboard navigation per WCAG 2.1.1 and 2.4.3.
functional_risks: Using capture-phase listener ensures our handler runs before VCP's, but could theoretically interfere with other capture-phase listeners on the input (unlikely in this codebase).

Calling hide() asynchronously means tabindex restoration happens after the keydown; however, the browser's default Tab action uses the tabindex state at the moment of the event. Since VCP sets tabindex=-1 when showing the calendar, and we stop VCP's preventDefault, the browser may still see tabindex=-1. However, hide() triggers VCP to restore tabindex synchronously during the hide call, so it should be restored before the browser processes the default action.
If the calendar is shown programmatically without user interaction, the Tab behavior remains unchanged.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Tab when the datepicker calendar is open moves focus to the passengers field.
Verify that pressing Tab when the datepicker calendar is closed still moves focus normally.
Verify that the calendar still functions correctly for date selection via mouse or keyboard.
Verify that the calendar hides appropriately when Tab is pressed.
Verify that no JavaScript errors are introduced.
Verify that Shift+Tab (reverse tab) still works correctly.
